body:
Fixes #446.

`PCF8563_Class::begin()` wrote `0x03` to Timer_control (`0x0E`). That cleared TE and changed TD, so a timer set before a reboot (`M5.Rtc.setTimerIRQ()` or `M5.Power.timerSleep(seconds)`) stopped as soon as `M5.begin()` ran. `cfg.disable_rtc_irq = false` did not help, because `M5.begin()` calls `Rtc.begin()` before it checks that option.

- `begin()` reads `0x0E` and leaves it unchanged while the timer is running (TE = 1). A stopped timer still gets `0x03` (TD = 1/60 Hz).
- `begin()` still fails when the `0x0E` access fails, as before.
- `disableIRQ()` writes `0x03` (TE off, TD = 1/60 Hz) instead of `0x00`. The datasheet asks for TD = 1/60 Hz while the timer is not used, for power saving. `setTimerIRQ(0)` already wrote `0x03`.

**Behavior change** (PCF8563 only; RX8130 is unchanged): with `cfg.disable_rtc_irq = false`, a timer set before the reboot now keeps running after `M5.begin()`. `clearIRQ()` alone does not stop it. Call `M5.Rtc.setTimerIRQ(0)` or `M5.Rtc.disableIRQ()` to stop it. The `disable_rtc_irq` comment says so. The default (`true`) still stops the timer in `M5.begin()`.

Tested on CoreInk (PCF8563). After setting a timer, `M5.Rtc.begin(&M5.In_I2C, M5.getBoard())` was called again (the same call `M5.begin()` makes):

| | Timer_control after `begin()` | timer flag after `begin()` |
|---|---|---|
| develop | `0x82` → `0x03` (stopped) | not set within 3x the period (1 s / 2 s) |
| this PR | `0x82` (unchanged) | set within one period (1 s / 2 s) |
| this PR, stopped timer left at `0x00` | `0x00` → `0x03` | — |

After `disableIRQ()`, Timer_control reads `0x03`. Fork CI passed.

Not tested: an actual power-off and RTC wake-up cycle on CoreInk, and the other boards with a PCF8563.
title: PCF8563: keep the timer running across begin()
